subject: Latency SLO carveout needed for semantic-ranker v0.9 (preview) — customer rollout plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Latency SLO carveout needed for semantic-ranker v0.9 (preview) — customer rollout plan

John —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme's search-relevance pilot looks promising and we're excited to support your rollout next month. Two items came up during planning that we need to formalize before the pilot:

1) The semantic-ranker model we discussed (v0.9, preview) is still in an optimized-but-not-final pipeline. For a phased roll we typically offer a temporary SLO carveout for preview models so teams can run production traffic while we stabilize latency and throughput.

2) You'll need an explicit, time-boxed exception on our side that documents the adjusted latency target, monitoring thresholds, and a rollback criterion if we see regressions.

Proposed approach we can start with:
- Temporary latency SLO: p95 <= 420ms (instead of our standard 250ms)
- Exception window: 6 weeks from pilot start date (with a 2-week canary first)
- Monitoring: token-level latency + error-rate alerting; weekly checkpoint calls

If that sounds reasonable, I can route the exception paperwork through our internal SLO review and share a DocuSign. Can you confirm the pilot start date (tentatively Mar 2) and whether procurement needs a separate statement of work?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: semantic-ranker-canary-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.ai>

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency SLO carveout needed for semantic-ranker v0.9 (preview) — customer rollout plan

Thanks Stephanie — this looks good at a high level. A few quick clarifications: 

- The proposed p95 420ms is acceptable for the canary phase. We do want to keep the canary limited to 10% of search traffic for the first two weeks.
- Procurement will need the exception in writing to attach to our internal change controls. They also asked if this will impact billing or credits if we exceed the temporary SLO — can you describe the remediation path?

On procurement: contracts@acme.ai will be the point of contact. They prefer a single PDF that includes the exception details and a brief canary plan.

John
Director of Product, Acme.ai

Subject: RE: Latency SLO carveout needed for semantic-ranker v0.9 (preview) — internal follow-up

Stephanie / Karthik —

Quick notes from infra/ops POV before we sign off on the exception paperwork: 

- Canary constraints: limiting to 10% traffic is fine; ops recommends scheduling the canary during low-peak hours for the first 48h to capture steady-state latencies.
- Observability: we'll enable token-level tracing and a p95 baseline for both the endpoint and the model KV cache hotpath; need the canary plan spreadsheet populated with expected QPS and sequence length distribution so autoscaler config can be tuned.
- Rollback criteria: suggest automatic rollback if p95 exceeds 700ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows or if error rate rises above 1.5%.

I've attached a lightweight SLO-exception template we use to capture the timeframe, altered SLOs, monitoring hooks, and owner contacts — can you push that to John and procurement?

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme_redwood_slo-exception-template.pdf (PDF stub)

Subject: Final: SLO exception + canary schedule for semantic-ranker v0.9 (preview)

Hi John / contracts team —

Per our discussions, attached is the one-page SLO exception document plus the canary plan workbook. Highlights:

- Temporary latency target: p95 <= 420ms for 6-week window (Mar 2 – Apr 13)
- Canary: first 2 weeks limited to 10% of search traffic; recommended low-peak start for first 48h
- Rollback: automatic rollback triggers if p95 > 700ms across two consecutive 5-minute windows OR error rate > 1.5%
- Monitoring: token-level latency tracing enabled, weekly checkpoints with Acme product and ops
- Billing: standard usage billing applies; no automatic credits for SLO breaches during the exception window. If an incident is root-caused to a Redwood runtime regression, we can discuss goodwill credits case-by-case — procurement noted for visibility.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm acceptance by replying to this thread (contracts@acme.ai is fine).
2) I'll upload the signed SLO-exception PDF to the HubSpot deal and send a DocuSign for signatures if you prefer that route.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk through the canary spreadsheet.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
